research_rationale:
EO 12580 (signed January 23, 1987; 52 FR 2923) implements the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (Superfund): it delegates the President's functions under the Act to the EPA Administrator and other agency heads (sections 1 to 9, 11), sets rules for Federal facilities (section 10), amends Executive Order 12088 (section 10(b)) and revokes Executive Order 12316 (section 11(h)). I read the complete held Federal Register original. I corrected the dossier inventory (79 clauses): the authority paragraph and paragraphs 11(f), (g) and (h), which print after the page break, are added; four pairs of OCR fragments that are single paragraphs are merged (2(g), 2(k), 4(c)(2), 10(b) with the inserted section 1-802); and one span is cut before a page header. Four held later orders amend it: EO 12777 (October 18, 1991) restated all of section 1 (before and after recorded in each section 1 clause, with a rewrite note), EO 13286 section 43 (effective March 1, 2003) changed the section 1(a)(2) agency list, EO 13016 (August 28, 1996) added subsections 4(c)(3) and 4(d)(3), and EO 13308 (June 20, 2003) revised section 1(b)(1), added subsections 5(f) and 5(g) and added sections 12 to 14. The held texts state no effective dates for EO 12777, 13016 and 13308, so their signing dates are recorded. Two clauses are one-time self-executing commands performed on signing, January 23, 1987: the amendment of EO 12088 (section 10(b)) and the revocation of EO 12316 (section 11(h)); both are recorded as terminated by performance. All other clauses are standing delegations or procedures with no end term and are operative, checked through 2026-10-14. The OFR disposition entry lists EO 12580 as amended by EO 12777, 13016, 13286 and 13308 and records no revocation; a March 2026 EPA rule (FR Doc. 2026-04904) applies the order as current; a USDA delegation rule (FR Doc. 2018-25443) cites it. The bounded searches record no revocation or supersession. Disclosed limit: the held texts do not show whether each delegated Act section is still the same section after later amendments of the Act; the claim rests on the absence of any held ending, not on a section-by-section check of the Act.
